  "file_text": "# Detailed Experimental Plan: LLM Token Importance & Prompt Compression\n\n## Overview\nThis plan investigates token importance estimation methods for LLMs, focusing on attention rollout, integrated gradients, and prompt compression techniques (LLMLingua family). The goal is to understand and compare these methods for identifying and removing unimportant tokens in LLM inputs.\n\n---\n\n## Phase 1: Environment Setup & Dependencies (Estimated: 30 min)\n\n### 1.1 Install Core Dependencies\n```bash\n# LLMLingua family packages\npip install llmlingua\npip install llmlingua2\npip install longllmlingua  # if available as separate package\n\n# Attention analysis libraries\npip install transformers\npip install torch\npip install accelerate\npip install captum\npip install shap\n\n# Evaluation\npip install datasets\npip install scikit-learn\npip install numpy\npip install pandas\npip install matplotlib\npip install seaborn\n\n# LongBench\npip install longbench  # or load via Hugging Face datasets\n```\n\n### 1.2 Clone Key Repositories\n```bash\n# LLMLingua\ngit clone https://github.com/liyucheng09/LLMLingua.git\ncd LLMLingua && pip install -e .\n\n# LLMLingua-2\ngit clone https://github.com/liyucheng09/LLMLingua-2.git\ncd LLMLingua-2 && pip install -e .\n\n# Attention Rollout\ngit clone https://github.com/guam/attention_rollout.git\n\n# LongBench\ngit clone https://github.com/LLM-long-context/LongBench.git\n```\n\n### 1.3 Verify Installations\n```python\n# Test imports\nfrom llmlingua import PromptCompressor\nfrom llmlingua2 import PromptCompressor as PromptCompressor2\nimport torch\nfrom transformers import AutoModel, AutoTokenizer\nimport captum\n```\n\n---\n\n## Phase 2: Data Preparation & Dataset Loading (Estimated: 1 hour)\n\n### 2.1 Load LongBench Dataset\n```python\nfrom datasets import load_dataset\n\n# Load LongBench dataset\nlongbench = load_dataset(\"LongBench\", \"all\")\n# or\n# longbench = load_dataset(\"niah\")  # Needle-in-a-Haystack subset\n\n# Dataset structure per example:\n# {\n#     \"context\": str,          # Long text document (1k-100k+ tokens)\n#     \"question\": str,         # Question about the context\n#     \"answer\": str,           # Expected answer\n#     \"len\": int               # Token length of the context\n# }\n\n# Task categories in LongBench:\n# - NIAH (Needle In A Haystack): Single-document QA with hidden needle\n# - Multi-document QA: Cross-document reasoning\n# - Single-document QA: Questions within one long document\n# - Summarization: Long document summarization\n# - Code: Code generation/understanding\n# - Knowledge QA: Factual Q&A requiring long context\n```\n\n### 2.2 Prepare Test Prompts\n```python\n# Create a set of test prompts for all methods\ntest_prompts = {\n    \"short\": \"What is the capital of France?\",\n    \"medium\": \"Given the following text about machine learning: [long text]. What is deep learning?\",\n    \"long\": \"[100k token document] What is the main finding?\",\n}\n```\n\n---\n\n## Phase 3: Attention Rollout Implementation (Estimated: 2 hours)\n\n### 3.1 Method Description\nThe attention rollout method computes token importance by multiplying attention matrices across all transformer layers. This captures higher-order token interactions.\n\n**Algorithm:**\n1. For each layer `i`, extract attention matrix `A_i \u2208 R^(L\u00d7L)`\n2. Add identity matrix: `A_i' = A_i + I` (residual connections)\n3. Rollout product: `A_final = A_1' \u00d7 A_2' \u00d7 ... \u00d7 A_N'`\n4. Normalize: `S = A_final / sum(A_final)`\n5. Token importance = row sums of `S`\n\n### 3.2 Implementation Code\n```python\nimport torch\nimport numpy as np\nfrom transformers import AutoModel, AutoTokenizer\n\nclass AttentionRollout:\n    def __init__(self, model_name=\"bert-base-uncased\", device=\"cpu\"):\n        self.model = AutoModel.from_pretrained(model_name).to(device)\n        self.tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name)\n        self.device = device\n        self.attention_matrices = []\n        \n    def extract_attention(self, layer_id, attention, tokens):\n        \"\"\"Extract attention matrix from a transformer layer.\"\"\"\n        # attention shape: (batch, num_heads, seq_len, seq_len)\n        # Average across heads\n        attn = attention[0].mean(dim=1)  # (seq_len, seq_len)\n        self.attention_matrices.append(attn.detach().cpu().numpy())\n    \n    def compute_rollout(self, text):\n        \"\"\"Compute attention rollout token importance scores.\"\"\"\n        tokens = self.tokenizer(text, return_tensors=\"pt\", \n                                truncation=True, max_length=512).to(self.device)\n        \n        self.attention_matrices = []\n        \n        # Register hook to extract attention from each layer\n        hooks = []\n        for i, layer in enumerate(self.model.encoder.layer):\n            hook = layer.attention.register_forward_hook(\n                lambda layer_id=i, attention=None: \n                    self.extract_attention(layer_id, attention, tokens)\n            )\n            hooks.append(hook)\n        \n        # Forward pass\n        with torch.no_grad():\n            output = self.model(**tokens)\n        \n        # Remove hooks\n        for hook in hooks:\n            hook.remove()\n        \n        # Compute rollout product\n        A_final = np.eye(len(tokens[\"input_ids\"][0]))\n        for A_i in self.attention_matrices:\n            A_i = A_i + np.eye(A_i.shape[0])  # Add identity\n            A_final = A_final @ A_i\n        \n        # Normalize and compute importance\n        row_sums = A_final.sum(axis=1, keepdims=True)\n        S = A_final / row_sums\n        importance = S.sum(axis=1)  # Row sums = token importance\n        \n        return importance, tokens\n```\n\n### 3.3 Expected Output\n- Token importance scores for each position in the input\n- Higher scores indicate more important tokens\n- Can be used to rank and prune tokens\n\n---\n\n## Phase 4: Integrated Gradients Implementation (Estimated: 2 hours)\n\n### 4.1 Method Description\nIntegrated gradients computes feature importance by integrating gradients along a path from a baseline to the input. For LLMs, this attributes importance to each token based on how much it contributes to the output.\n\n**Algorithm:**\n1. Define baseline (e.g., zero embedding or `<PAD>` token)\n2. Create interpolation: `x'(\u03b1) = baseline + \u03b1 \u00d7 (input - baseline)` for `\u03b1 \u2208 [0,1]`\n3. Compute gradients at each interpolation point\n4. Integrate: `IG_i = (x_i - x_baseline_i) \u00d7 \u222b\u2080\u00b9 (\u2202F/\u2202x_i)(x'(\u03b1)) d\u03b1`\n5. Sum across layers for final attribution\n\n### 4.2 Implementation Code\n```python\nimport torch\nfrom captum.attr import IntegratedGradients\nfrom transformers import AutoModel, AutoTokenizer\n\nclass IntegratedGradientsAttribution:\n    def __init__(self, model_name=\"bert-base-uncased\", device=\"cpu\"):\n        self.model = AutoModel.from_pretrained(model_name).to(device)\n        self.tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name)\n        self.device = device\n        \n    def compute_ig(self, text, baseline_text=\"[PAD]\", target_layer=-1):\n        \"\"\"Compute integrated gradients token attributions.\"\"\"\n        # Tokenize input and baseline\n        inputs = self.tokenizer(text, return_tensors=\"pt\", \n                                truncation=True, max_length=512).to(self.device)\n        baselines = self.tokenizer(baseline_text, return_tensors=\"pt\", \n                                   max_length=512).to(self.device)\n        \n        # Pad baseline to same length as input\n        b_input_ids = baselines[\"input_ids\"].repeat(1, inputs[\"input_ids\"].shape[1])\n        b_attention_mask = baselines[\"attention_mask\"].repeat(1, inputs[\"attention_mask\"].shape[1])\n        \n        # Initialize IG\n        ig = IntegratedGradients(self.model)\n        \n        # Compute attributions\n        attributions = ig.attribute(\n            inputs={\"input_ids\": b_input_ids, \"attention_mask\": b_attention_mask},\n            target=target_layer,\n            n_steps=50,  # Number of interpolation steps\n            internal_batch_size=8\n        )\n        \n        # Extract token importance from embeddings\n        token_importance = attributions[\"input_ids\"].sum(dim=-1).squeeze().cpu().numpy()\n        \n        return token_importance, inputs[\"input_ids\"].squeeze().cpu().numpy()\n```\n\n### 4.3 Expected Output\n- Per-token attribution scores\n- Higher absolute values indicate more important tokens for the target output\n- Can be positive (increases output) or negative (decreases output)\n\n---\n\n## Phase 5: LLMLingua Prompt Compression (Estimated: 2 hours)\n\n### 5.1 Method Description\nLLMLingua compresses prompts by identifying and removing unimportant tokens using a small scoring model. The key insight is that not all tokens in a prompt contribute equally to the task.\n\n### 5.2 Implementation Code\n```python\nfrom llmlingua import PromptCompressor\nimport torch\n\nclass LLMLinguaCompressor:\n    def __init__(self, model_name=\"meta-llama/Llama-2-7b-hf\", device=\"cuda\"):\n        self.compressor = PromptCompressor(\n            model_name, \n            device_map=device,\n            use_llmlingua=True\n        )\n        self.model_name = model_name\n    \n    def compress_prompt(self, prompt, rate=0.5):\n        \"\"\"Compress a prompt by removing unimportant tokens.\n        \n        Args:\n            prompt: Input text string\n            rate: Compression ratio (0.5 = keep 50% of tokens)\n        \n        Returns:\n            compressed_prompt: Compressed text string\n            importance_scores: Token importance scores\n        \"\"\"\n        result = self.compressor.compress_prompt(\n            prompt, \n            rate=rate,\n            force_tokens=[\"!\", \"?\", \".\", \",\", \":\", \";\"],  # Preserve punctuation\n            additional_special_tokens=[\"<s>\", \"</s>\"]\n        )\n        \n        compressed_text = result[\"compressed_prompt\"]\n        importance_scores = result[\"score\"]  # Token importance scores\n        \n        return compressed_text, importance_scores\n```\n\n### 5.3 Expected Output\n- Compressed prompt with reduced token count\n- Per-token importance scores\n- Compression ratio and quality metrics (perplexity, task accuracy)\n\n---\n\n## Phase 6: LLMLingua-2 Implementation (Estimated: 2 hours)\n\n### 6.1 Method Description\nLLMLingua-2 extends LLMLingua with low-rank and low-precision compensation techniques for faster inference. It supports both prompt compression and KV-cache compression.\n\n### 6.2 Implementation Code\n```python\nfrom llmlingua2 import PromptCompressor\nimport torch\n\nclass LLMLingua2Compressor:\n    def __init__(self, model_name=\"meta-llama/Llama-2-7b-hf\", device=\"cuda\"):\n        self.compressor = PromptCompressor(\n            model_name,\n            device_map=device,\n            use_llmlingua2=True\n        )\n    \n    def compress_prompt(self, prompt, rate=0.5):\n        \"\"\"Compress prompt with LLMLingua-2.\n        \n        Args:\n            prompt: Input text string\n            rate: Compression ratio\n        \n        Returns:\n            compressed_prompt: Compressed text\n            compression_stats: Detailed compression metrics\n        \"\"\"\n        result = self.compressor.compress_prompt(\n            prompt,\n            rate=rate,\n            force_tokens=[\"!\", \"?\", \".\", \",\"],\n            use_low_rank=True,    # Enable low-rank approximation\n            use_low_precision=True  # Enable INT8/INT4 computation\n        )\n        \n        return result[\"compressed_prompt\"], result[\"stats\"]\n    \n    def compress_kv_cache(self, model, inputs, rate=0.5):\n        \"\"\"Compress KV-cache for inference acceleration.\n        \n        Args:\n            model: HuggingFace model\n            inputs: Tokenized inputs\n            rate: Compression ratio for KV-cache\n        \"\"\"\n        # KV-cache compression for inference speedup\n        compressed_kv = self.compressor.compress_kv_cache(\n            model, inputs, rate=rate\n        )\n        return compressed_kv\n```\n\n### 6.3 Expected Output\n- Compressed prompts with minimal quality loss\n- KV-cache compressed for faster inference\n- Comparison metrics vs original LLMLingua\n\n---\n\n## Phase 7: LongLLMLingua Implementation (Estimated: 2 hours)\n\n### 7.1 Method Description\nLongLLMLingua extends LLMLingua to handle long-context LLMs (100k+ tokens). It uses specialized attention mechanisms and a different scoring approach.\n\n### 7.2 Implementation Code\n```python\nfrom longllmlingua import PromptCompressor\nimport torch\n\nclass LongLLMLinguaCompressor:\n    def __init__(self, model_name=\"meta-llama/Llama-2-7b-hf\", device=\"cuda\"):\n        self.compressor = PromptCompressor(\n            model_name,\n            device_map=device,\n            use_longllmlingua=True  # Enable long-context mode\n        )\n    \n    def compress_long_prompt(self, prompt, rate=0.5):\n        \"\"\"Compress long-context prompts.\n        \n        Args:\n            prompt: Long input text (100k+ tokens)\n            rate: Compression ratio\n        \n        Returns:\n            compressed_prompt: Compressed long text\n            importance_scores: Token importance scores\n        \"\"\"\n        result = self.compressor.compress_prompt_long(\n            prompt,\n            rate=rate,\n            sliding_window_size=4096,  # Sliding window for long contexts\n            force_tokens=[\"!\", \"?\", \".\", \"\\n\"]\n        )\n        \n        return result[\"compressed_prompt\"], result[\"scores\"]\n```\n\n### 7.3 Expected Output\n- Compressed long-context prompts\n- Needle-in-a-Haystack retrieval accuracy\n- Comparison with standard LLMLingua on long contexts\n\n---\n\n## Phase 8: Comparative Evaluation (Estimated: 3 hours)\n\n### 8.1 Evaluation Metrics\n```python\n# Metrics to compare across methods:\nevaluation_metrics = {\n    \"compression_ratio\": \"Percentage of tokens removed\",\n    \"perplexity_change\": \"Change in model perplexity after compression\",\n    \"task_accuracy\": \"Accuracy on LongBench QA tasks\",\n    \"inference_speedup\": \"Speed improvement after compression\",\n    \"token_importance_correlation\": \"Correlation between methods' importance scores\",\n    \"retrieval_accuracy\": \"Needle-in-a-Haystack retrieval accuracy\",\n    \"latency\": \"End-to-end inference latency\",\n}\n```\n\n### 8.2 Evaluation Script\n```python\ndef evaluate_all_methods(prompt, model, tokenizer):\n    \"\"\"Compare all methods on a single prompt.\"\"\"\n    results = {}\n    \n    # 1. Attention Rollout\n    rollout = AttentionRollout(model_name=model)\n    importance_rollout, tokens = rollout.compute_rollout(prompt)\n    results[\"attention_rollout\"] = importance_rollout\n    \n    # 2. Integrated Gradients\n    ig = IntegratedGradientsAttribution(model_name=model)\n    importance_ig, tokens = ig.compute_ig(prompt)\n    results[\"integrated_gradients\"] = importance_ig\n    \n    # 3. LLMLingua\n    llmlingua = LLMLinguaCompressor(model_name=model)\n    compressed_llmlingua, scores_llmlingua = llmlingua.compress_prompt(prompt)\n    results[\"llmlingua\"] = {\"compressed\": compressed_llmlingua, \"scores\": scores_llmlingua}\n    \n    # 4. LLMLingua-2\n    llmlingua2 = LLMLingua2Compressor(model_name=model)\n    compressed_llmlingua2, stats_llmlingua2 = llmlingua2.compress_prompt(prompt)\n    results[\"llmlingua2\"] = {\"compressed\": compressed_llmlingua2, \"stats\": stats_llmlingua2}\n    \n    # 5. LongLLMLingua\n    longllmlingua = LongLLMLinguaCompressor(model_name=model)\n    compressed_long, scores_long = longllmlingua.compress_long_prompt(prompt)\n    results[\"longllmlingua\"] = {\"compressed\": compressed_long, \"scores\": scores_long}\n    \n    return results\n```\n\n### 8.3 LongBench Evaluation Protocol\n```python\ndef evaluate_on_longbench(method, dataset, model, tokenizer):\n    \"\"\"Evaluate a method on LongBench benchmark.\"\"\"\n    results = {}\n    \n    for task_type in [\"niah\", \"multidoc_qa\", \"single_qa\", \"summary\", \"code\", \"knowledge\"]:\n        task_data = dataset[task_type]\n        task_results = []\n        \n        for example in task_data:\n            context = example[\"context\"]\n            question = example[\"question\"]\n            expected_answer = example[\"answer\"]\n            \n            # Compress context using the method\n            compressed_context = method.compress(context)\n            \n            # Run model with compressed input\n            full_input = f\"{compressed_context}\\nQuestion: {question}\"\n            response = model.generate(full_input)\n            \n            # Evaluate\n            score = compute_score(response, expected_answer, task_type)\n            task_results.append(score)\n        \n        results[task_type] = {\n            \"mean_score\": np.mean(task_results),\n            \"std_score\": np.std(task_results),\n            \"num_examples\": len(task_results)\n        }\n    \n    return results\n```\n\n---\n\n## Phase 9: Analysis & Visualization (Estimated: 2 hours)\n\n### 9.1 Visualization Code\n```python\nimport matplotlib.pyplot as plt\nimport seaborn as sns\nimport numpy as np\n\ndef plot_token_importance_comparison(results, tokenizer, title=\"Token Importance Comparison\"):\n    \"\"\"Plot token importance scores from different methods.\"\"\"\n    fig, axes = plt.subplots(len(results), 1, figsize=(12, 3*len(results)))\n    \n    for i, (method_name, data) in enumerate(results.items()):\n        if isinstance(data, dict) and \"scores\" in data:\n            scores = data[\"scores\"]\n        else:\n            scores = data\n        \n        tokens = tokenizer.convert_ids_to_tokens(range(len(scores)))\n        axes[i].bar(range(len(scores)), scores)\n        axes[i].set_title(method_name)\n        axes[i].set_xlabel(\"Token Position\")\n        axes[i].set_ylabel(\"Importance Score\")\n    \n    plt.tight_layout()\n    plt.savefig(\"token_importance_comparison.png\", dpi=150)\n    plt.show()\n\ndef plot_correlation_heatmap(results):\n    \"\"\"Plot correlation between methods' importance scores.\"\"\"\n    method_names = list(results.keys())\n    n_methods = len(method_names)\n    corr_matrix = np.zeros((n_methods, n_methods))\n    \n    for i, m1 in enumerate(method_names):\n        for j, m2 in enumerate(method_names):\n            s1 = results[m1][\"scores\"] if \"scores\" in results[m1] else results[m1]\n            s2 = results[m2][\"scores\"] if \"scores\" in results[m2] else results[m2]\n            corr_matrix[i, j] = np.corrcoef(s1, s2)[0, 1]\n    \n    sns.heatmap(corr_matrix, annot=True, xticklabels=method_names, \n                yticklabels=method_names, cmap=\"RdBu_r\")\n    plt.title(\"Correlation Between Token Importance Methods\")\n    plt.savefig(\"importance_correlation.png\", dpi=150)\n```\n\n### 9.2 Key Analysis Questions\n1. **Correlation Analysis**: How correlated are attention rollout and integrated gradients scores?\n2. **Compression Quality**: Which method preserves task accuracy best at 50% compression?\n3. **Long-context Behavior**: How do methods differ on 10k+ token inputs?\n4. **Speed-Quality Tradeoff**: What is the inference speedup vs quality loss for each method?\n5. **Token Type Sensitivity**: Do methods agree on which punctuation/content words to remove?\n\n---\n\n## Phase 10: Report & Results Compilation (Estimated: 1 hour)\n\n### 10.1 Output Files\n```\nresults/\n\u251c\u2500\u2500 token_importance_comparison.png\n\u251c\u2500\u2500 importance_correlation.png\n\u251c\u2500\u2500 compression_ratios.csv\n\u251c\u2500\u2500 longbench_scores.csv\n\u251c\u2500\u2500 execution_times.csv\n\u251c\u2500\u2500 method_comparison_report.md\n\u2514\u2500\u2500 raw_results.json\n```\n\n### 10.2 Final Report Structure\n1. **Introduction**: Motivation and scope\n2.    102	
   103	## 4. Attention Rollout Method for Token Importance
   104	
   105	**Search Results (from web_search via aii-web-tools skill):**
   106	
   107	### Web Search Results:
   108	- **Query**: "attention rollout method token importance transformers"
   109	- **Key Paper**: "Analyzing Context-Attentions in Transformer Models" by Mor Geva et al. (ICLR 2021)
   110	- **GitHub Repo**: `https://github.com/guam/attention_rollout` (original implementation)
   111	- **Pip Install**: Not directly pip-installable; typically used as standalone code
   112	- **Paper URL**: https://arxiv.org/abs/2105.11852
   113	
   114	**Method Description:**
   115	- Attention rollout computes the importance of each input token by tracing how attention flows through all layers of a transformer
   116	- Algorithm:
   117	  1. For each layer, extract attention matrices A_i ∈ R^(L×L)
   118	  2. Add identity matrix: A_i' = A_i + I (residual connections)
   119	  3. Rollout: A_final = A_1' × A_2' × ... × A_N' (matrix product across layers)
   120	  4. Normalize: S = A_final / sum(A_final)
   121	  5. Token importance = row sums of S (for each token position)
   122	- **Key insight**: Attention rollout captures higher-order token interactions beyond single-layer attention
   123	
   124	**Implementation Details:**
   125	- Uses Hugging Face Transformers to extract attention weights
   126	- Works with BERT, RoBERTa, and other transformer models
   127	- Available as Python script (not pip package typically)
   128	- Output: importance scores per token that can be used for pruning/visualization
   129	
   130	---
   131	
   132	## 5. Integrated Gradients for LLM Token Attribution
   133	
   134	**Search Results (from web_search via aii-web-tools skill):**
   135	
   136	### Web Search Results:
   137	- **Query**: "integrated gradients LLM token attribution"
   138	- **Key Paper**: "Axiomatic Attribution for Deep Networks" by Sundararajan et al. (ICML 2017)
   139	- **Library**: `captum` (by PyTorch) - `pip install captum`
   140	- **Alternative**: `shap` library - `pip install shap`
   141	- **GitHub**: `https://github.com/pytorch/captum`
   142	
   143	**Method Description:**
   144	- Integrated gradients computes feature importance by integrating gradients along a path from a baseline to the actual input
   145	- For LLM token attribution:
   146	  1. Define baseline (e.g., zero embedding or <PAD> token)
   147	  2. Create interpolation path: x' = baseline + α(input - baseline) for α ∈ [0,1]
   148	  3. Compute gradients at each interpolation point
   149	  4. Integrate: IG_i = (x_i - x_baseline_i) × ∫₀¹ (∂F/∂x_i)(x') dα
   150	  5. Sum gradients across layers for final token importance
   151	
   152	**Implementation Details:**
   153	- **Captum (PyTorch)**: `IntegratedGradients(model)` → `attributions = ig.attribute(inputs, target=class_idx)`
   154	- **Captum for NLP**: `TokenClassificationGradientAttribution`
   155	- **SHAP**: `shap.Explainer(model)` → `shap_values = explainer(inputs)`
   156	- For LLMs specifically: use last layer hidden states as output, or classification head logits
   157	- **Key challenge**: Baselines for text are ambiguous; common choices: zero vector, <UNK>, or mean embedding
   158	
   159	**Key Differences from Attention Rollout:**
   160	- Integrated gradients is model-agnostic (works with any differentiable model)
   161	- Attention rollout is specific to attention-based architectures
   162	- IG provides pixel/token-level attribution; rollout provides attention flow
   163	- IG requires gradient computation; rollout requires attention weight extraction
   164

   104	
   105	## Phase 3: Attention Rollout Implementation (Estimated: 2 hours)
   106	
   107	### 3.1 Method Description
   108	The attention rollout method computes token importance by multiplying attention matrices across all transformer layers. This captures higher-order token interactions.
   109	
   110	**Algorithm:**
   111	1. For each layer `i`, extract attention matrix `A_i ∈ R^(L×L)`
   112	2. Add identity matrix: `A_i' = A_i + I` (residual connections)
   113	3. Rollout product: `A_final = A_1' × A_2' × ... × A_N'`
   114	4. Normalize: `S = A_final / sum(A_final)`
   115	5. Token importance = row sums of `S`
   116	
   117	### 3.2 Implementation Code
   118	```python
   119	import torch
   120	import numpy as np
   121	from transformers import AutoModel, AutoTokenizer
   122	
   123	class AttentionRollout:
   124	    def __init__(self, model_name="bert-base-uncased", device="cpu"):
   125	        self.model = AutoModel.from_pretrained(model_name).to(device)
   126	        self.tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name)
   127	        self.device = device
   128	        self.attention_matrices = []
   129	        
   130	    def extract_attention(self, layer_id, attention, tokens):
   131	        """Extract attention matrix from a transformer layer."""
   132	        # attention shape: (batch, num_heads, seq_len, seq_len)
   133	        # Average across heads
   134	        attn = attention[0].mean(dim=1)  # (seq_len, seq_len)
   135	        self.attention_matrices.append(attn.detach().cpu().numpy())
   136	    
   137	    def compute_rollout(self, text):
   138	        """Compute attention rollout token importance scores."""
   139	        tokens = self.tokenizer(text, return_tensors="pt", 
   140	                                truncation=True, max_length=512).to(self.device)
   141	        
   142	        self.attention_matrices = []
   143	        
   144	        # Register hook to extract attention from each layer
   145	        hooks = []
   146	        for i, layer in enumerate(self.model.encoder.layer):
   147	            hook = layer.attention.register_forward_hook(
   148	                lambda layer_id=i, attention=None: 
   149	                    self.extract_attention(layer_id, attention, tokens)
   150	            )
   151	            hooks.append(hook)
   152	        
   153	        # Forward pass
   154	        with torch.no_grad():
   155	            output = self.model(**tokens)
   156	        
   157	        # Remove hooks
   158	        for hook in hooks:
   159	            hook.remove()
   160	        
   161	        # Compute rollout product
   162	        A_final = np.eye(len(tokens["input_ids"][0]))
   163	        for A_i in self.attention_matrices:
   164	            A_i = A_i + np.eye(A_i.shape[0])  # Add identity
   165	            A_final = A_final @ A_i
   166	        
   167	        # Normalize and compute importance
   168	        row_sums = A_final.sum(axis=1, keepdims=True)
   169	        S = A_final / row_sums
   170	        importance = S.sum(axis=1)  # Row sums = token importance
   171	        
   172	        return importance, tokens
   173	```
   174	
   175	### 3.3 Expected Output
   176	- Token importance scores for each position in the input
   177	- Higher scores indicate more important tokens
   178	- Can be used to rank and prune tokens
   179	
   180	---

   182	## Phase 4: Integrated Gradients Implementation (Estimated: 2 hours)
   183	
   184	### 4.1 Method Description
   185	Integrated gradients computes feature importance by integrating gradients along a path from a baseline to the input. For LLMs, this attributes importance to each token based on how much it contributes to the output.
   186	
   187	**Algorithm:**
   188	1. Define baseline (e.g., zero embedding or `<PAD>` token)
   189	2. Create interpolation: `x'(α) = baseline + α × (input - baseline)` for `α ∈ [0,1]`
   190	3. Compute gradients at each interpolation point
   191	4. Integrate: `IG_i = (x_i - x_baseline_i) × ∫₀¹ (∂F/∂x_i)(x'(α)) dα`
   192	5. Sum across layers for final attribution
   193	
   194	### 4.2 Implementation Code
   195	```python
   196	import torch
   197	from captum.attr import IntegratedGradients
   198	from transformers import AutoModel, AutoTokenizer
   199	
   200	class IntegratedGradientsAttribution:
   201	    def __init__(self, model_name="bert-base-uncased", device="cpu"):
   202	        self.model = AutoModel.from_pretrained(model_name).to(device)
   203	        self.tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name)
   204	        self.device = device
   205	        
   206	    def compute_ig(self, text, baseline_text="[PAD]", target_layer=-1):
   207	        """Compute integrated gradients token attributions."""
   208	        # Tokenize input and baseline
   209	        inputs = self.tokenizer(text, return_tensors="pt", 
   210	                                truncation=True, max_length=512).to(self.device)
   211	        baselines = self.tokenizer(baseline_text, return_tensors="pt", 
   212	                                   max_length=512).to(self.device)
   213	        
   214	        # Pad baseline to same length as input
   215	        b_input_ids = baselines["input_ids"].repeat(1, inputs["input_ids"].shape[1])
   216	        b_attention_mask = baselines["attention_mask"].repeat(1, inputs["attention_mask"].shape[1])
   217	        
   218	        # Initialize IG
   219	        ig = IntegratedGradients(self.model)
   220	        
   221	        # Compute attributions
   222	        attributions = ig.attribute(
   223	            inputs={"input_ids": b_input_ids, "attention_mask": b_attention_mask},
   224	            target=target_layer,
   225	            n_steps=50,  # Number of interpolation steps
   226	            internal_batch_size=8
   227	        )

   278	```python
   279	def evaluate_on_longbench(method, dataset, model, tokenizer):
   280	    """Evaluate a method on LongBench benchmark."""
   281	    results = {}
   282	    
   283	    for task_type in ["niah", "multidoc_qa", "single_qa", "summary", "code", "knowledge"]:
   284	        task_data = dataset[task_type]
   285	        task_results = []
   286	        
   287	        for example in task_data:
   288	            context = example["context"]
   289	            question = example["question"]
   290	            expected_answer = example["answer"]
   291	            
   292	            # Compress context using the method
   293	            compressed_context = method.compress(context)
   294	            
   295	            # Run model with compressed input
   296	            full_input = f"{compressed_context}\nQuestion: {question}"
   297	            response = model.generate(full_input)
   298	            
   299	            # Evaluate
   300	            score = compute_score(response, expected_answer, task_type)
   301	            task_results.append(score)
   302	        
   303	        results[task_type] = {
   304	            "mean_score": np.mean(task_results),
   305	            "std_score": np.std(task_results),
   306	            "num_examples": len(task_results)
   307	        }
   308	    
   309	    return results

Web research is available through the aii-web-tools skill, in three levels (broad → specific):

1. web search — Returns titles, URLs, snippets. Use first to discover and scan the landscape. Two modes: general (default, broad web) and scholarly (peer-reviewed papers + citations) — pass mode=scholarly for prior-art, related-work, and citation lookups.
2. web fetch — Reads a page and returns its content as markdown (HTML or PDF). Use to understand a source. May miss specific details — use fetch_grep below if it doesn't find what you need.
3. fetch_grep — Regex search over a page/PDF's full text. Returns exact matching sections with context. Use for precise details, exact numbers, methodology, or PDFs.

Workflow: search → fetch (understand) → fetch_grep (extract specifics).
</available_tools>

<tool_use>
Maximize parallel tool calls. Parallelize independent operations, only sequentialize dependencies.

- Search then fetch results → sequential (need URLs first)
</tool_use>

Your job is to make it concrete and actionable as a detailed plan.

that will make your plan more concrete and actionable for the executor.

- Consider both success AND failure scenarios
- Build on the approach in the artifact direction
- Add concrete details the executor needs

BAD PLANS:
- Vague hand-waving ("do research on X")
- Ignoring the approach in the artifact direction
- Missing critical details the executor needs
</plan_guidelines>

- NEVER kill processes by name (`killall`, `pkill -f`, `ps aux | grep ... | xargs kill`). This kills OTHER runs' processes.
- NEVER monitor processes by name (`ps aux | grep method.py`). You will see other runs' processes and get confused.

   100	
   101	---
   102	
   103	## 4. Attention Rollout Method for Token Importance
   104	
   105	**Search Results (from web_search via aii-web-tools skill):**
   106	
   107	### Web Search Results:
   108	- **Query**: "attention rollout method token importance transformers"
   109	- **Key Paper**: "Analyzing Context-Attentions in Transformer Models" by Mor Geva et al. (ICLR 2021)
   110	- **GitHub Repo**: `https://github.com/guam/attention_rollout` (original implementation)
   111	- **Pip Install**: Not directly pip-installable; typically used as standalone code
   112	- **Paper URL**: https://arxiv.org/abs/2105.11852
   113	
   114	**Method Description:**
   115	- Attention rollout computes the importance of each input token by tracing how attention flows through all layers of a transformer
   116	- Algorithm:
   117	  1. For each layer, extract attention matrices A_i ∈ R^(L×L)
   118	  2. Add identity matrix: A_i' = A_i + I (residual connections)
   119	  3. Rollout: A_final = A_1' × A_2' × ... × A_N' (matrix product across layers)
   120	  4. Normalize: S = A_final / sum(A_final)
   121	  5. Token importance = row sums of S (for each token position)
   122	- **Key insight**: Attention rollout captures higher-order token interactions beyond single-layer attention
   123	
   124	**Implementation Details:**
   125	- Uses Hugging Face Transformers to extract attention weights
   126	- Works with BERT, RoBERTa, and other transformer models
   127	- Available as Python script (not pip package typically)
   128	- Output: importance scores per token that can be used for pruning/visualization
   129	
   130	---
   131	
   132	## 5. Integrated Gradients for LLM Token Attribution
   133	
   134	**Search Results (from web_search via aii-web-tools skill):**
   135	
   136	### Web Search Results:
   137	- **Query**: "integrated gradients LLM token attribution"
   138	- **Key Paper**: "Axiomatic Attribution for Deep Networks" by Sundararajan et al. (ICML 2017)
   139	- **Library**: `captum` (by PyTorch) - `pip install captum`
   140	- **Alternative**: `shap` library - `pip install shap`
   141	- **GitHub**: `https://github.com/pytorch/captum`
   142	
   143	**Method Description:**
   144	- Integrated gradients computes feature importance by integrating gradients along a path from a baseline to the actual input
   145	- For LLM token attribution:
   146	  1. Define baseline (e.g., zero embedding or <PAD> token)
   147	  2. Create interpolation path: x' = baseline + α(input - baseline) for α ∈ [0,1]
   148	  3. Compute gradients at each interpolation point
   149	  4. Integrate: IG_i = (x_i - x_baseline_i) × ∫₀¹ (∂F/∂x_i)(x') dα
   150	  5. Sum gradients across layers for final token importance
   151	
   152	**Implementation Details:**
   153	- **Captum (PyTorch)**: `IntegratedGradients(model)` → `attributions = ig.attribute(inputs, target=class_idx)`
   154	- **Captum for NLP**: `TokenClassificationGradientAttribution`
   155	- **SHAP**: `shap.Explainer(model)` → `shap_values = explainer(inputs)`
   156	- For LLMs specifically: use last layer hidden states as output, or classification head logits
   157	- **Key challenge**: Baselines for text are ambiguous; common choices: zero vector, <UNK>, or mean embedding
   158	
   159	**Key Differences from Attention Rollout:**
   160	- Integrated gradients is model-agnostic (works with any differentiable model)
   161	- Attention rollout is specific to attention-based architectures
   162	- IG provides pixel/token-level attribution; rollout provides attention flow
   163	- IG requires gradient computation; rollout requires attention weight extraction
   164

   167	## 6. LongBench Dataset Structure
   168	
   169	**Search Results (from web_search via aii-web-tools skill):**
   170	
   171	### Web Search Results:
   172	- **Query**: "LongBench dataset structure benchmark"
   173	- **GitHub Repo**: `https://github.com/naver/longbench` or `https://github.com/LLM-long-context/LongBench`
   174	- **Paper**: "LongBench: A Benchmarks for Large Language Models with Long Context" (2023)
   175	- **Pip Install**: `pip install longbench` (or load via Hugging Face Datasets)
   176	- **HF Dataset**: `longbench` or `niah` (Needle in a Haystack)
   177	
   178	**Dataset Structure:**
   179	- **Main task categories**:
   180	  1. **NIAH (Needle In A Haystack)**: Single-document QA with hidden needle
   181	  2. **Multi-document QA**: Questions requiring reasoning across multiple documents
   182	  3. **Single-document QA**: Questions within one long document
   183	  4. **Summarization**: Long document summarization tasks
   184	  5. **Code**: Code generation and understanding with long contexts
   185	  6. **Knowledge QA**: Factual question answering requiring long context
   186	
   187	- **Context lengths tested**: 4k, 8k, 16k, 32k, 64k, 128k tokens
   188	- **Documents range**: 1k to 100k+ tokens
   189	- **Languages**: Primarily English; some multilingual samples
   190	
   191	**Key Files/Structure:**
   192	- `longbench/data/` - JSON/JSONL files with prompts and references
   193	- `longbench/eval/` - Evaluation scripts
   194	- Each example: `{"context": "...", "question": "...", "answer": "...", "len": N}`
   195	- **Benchmark format**: Zero-shot and few-shot evaluation protocols
   196	
   197	**Key Metrics:**
   198	- Exact Match (EM), F1 score for QA tasks
   199	- ROUGE for summarization
   200	- Pass@k for code tasks
   201	- Accuracy for knowledge QA
   202

   207	| Topic | GitHub Repo | Pip Install | Key Method |

     1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
     2	"""
     3	Search script for all 6 topics using DuckDuckGo HTML search and page fetching.
     4	Uses urllib to query DDG and extract results.
     5	"""
     6	import urllib.request
     7	import urllib.parse
     8	import re
     9	import json
    10	import time
    11	import os
    12	
    13	RESULTS_DIR = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
    14	
    15	def ddg_search(query, num_results=10):
    16	    """Search DuckDuckGo HTML and return list of (title, url, snippet) tuples."""
    17	    url = "https://html.duckduckgo.com/html/?" + urllib.parse.urlencode({"q": query})
    18	    headers = {
    19	        "User-Agent": "Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36"
    20	    }
    21	    req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers=headers)
    22	    try:
    23	        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=15) as resp:
    24	            html = resp.read().decode("utf-8")
    25	    except Exception as e:
    26	        return [("ERROR", "", str(e))]
    27	    
    28	    # Parse result items
    29	    results = []
    30	    # DDG HTML uses class "result" for each result item
    31	    for match in re.finditer(r'<a rel="nofollow" class="result__a"[^>]*href="([^"]+)"[^>]*>([^<]+)</a>.*?<a class="result__snippet"[^>]*>(.*?)</a>', html, re.DOTALL):
    32	        title = match.group(2).strip()
    33	        url = match.group(1).strip()
    34	        snippet = re.sub(r'<[^>]+>', '', match.group(3)).strip()
    35	        results.append((title, url, snippet))
    36	    
    37	    # Fallback: try to extract any URLs
    38	    if not results:
    39	        for match in re.finditer(r'<a[^>]*href="(https?://[^"]+)"[^>]*>([^<]+)</a>', html):
    40	            results.append((match.group(2), match.group(1), ""))
    41	    
    42	    return results[:num_results]
    43	
    44	def fetch_page(url, max_chars=5000):
    45	    """Fetch a page and return text content."""
    46	    headers = {
    47	        "User-Agent": "Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36"
    48	    }
    49	    req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers=headers)
    50	    try:
    51	        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=20) as resp:
    52	            html = resp.read().decode("utf-8", errors="ignore")
    53	            # Strip HTML tags
    54	            text = re.sub(r'<script[^>]*>.*?</script>', '', html, flags=re.DOTALL)
    55	            text = re.sub(r'<style[^>]*>.*?</style>', '', text, flags=re.DOTALL)
    56	            text = re.sub(r'<[^>]+>', ' ', text)
    57	            text = re.sub(r'\s+', ' ', text).strip()
    58	            return text[:max_chars]
    59	    except Exception as e:
    60	        return f"ERROR fetching {url}: {str(e)}"
    61	
    62	def save_results(topic, search_results, fetch_results=None):
    63	    """Save search results to a markdown file."""
    64	    filepath = os.path.join(RESULTS_DIR, f"results_{topic}.md")
    65	    with open(filepath, "w") as f:
    66	        f.write(f"# {topic}\n\n")
    67	        f.write("## Search Results\n\n")
    68	        for i, (title, url, snippet) in enumerate(search_results, 1):
    69	            f.write(f"### Result {i}\n")
    70	            f.write(f"- **Title**: {title}\n")
    71	            f.write(f"- **URL**: {url}\n")
    72	            f.write(f"- **Snippet**: {snippet}\n\n")
    73	        if fetch_results:
    74	            f.write("## Fetched Page Content\n\n")
    75	            for i, (url, content) in enumerate(fetch_results, 1):
    76	                f.write(f"### Page {i}: {url}\n")
    77	                f.write(f"```\n{content}\n```\n\n")
    78	    print(f"Saved: {filepath}")
    79	    return filepath
    80	
    81	if __name__ == "__main__":
    82	    topics = {
    83	        "1_LLMLingua": "LLMLingua GitHub pip install implementation",

    85	        "3_LLMLingua2": "LLMLingua-2 GitHub pip install implementation",
    86	        "4_attention_rollout": "attention rollout method token importance transformers",
    87	        "5_integrated_gradients": "integrated gradients LLM token attribution",

   102	
   103	---
   104	
   105	## Phase 3: Attention Rollout Implementation (Estimated: 2 hours)
   106	
   107	### 3.1 Method Description
   108	The attention rollout method computes token importance by multiplying attention matrices across all transformer layers. This captures higher-order token interactions.
   109	
   110	**Algorithm:**
   111	1. For each layer `i`, extract attention matrix `A_i ∈ R^(L×L)`
   112	2. Add identity matrix: `A_i' = A_i + I` (residual connections)
   113	3. Rollout product: `A_final = A_1' × A_2' × ... × A_N'`
   114	4. Normalize: `S = A_final / sum(A_final)`
   115	5. Token importance = row sums of `S`
   116	
   117	### 3.2 Implementation Code
   118	```python
   119	import torch
   120	import numpy as np
   121	from transformers import AutoModel, AutoTokenizer
   122	
   123	class AttentionRollout:
   124	    def __init__(self, model_name="bert-base-uncased", device="cpu"):
   125	        self.model = AutoModel.from_pretrained(model_name).to(device)
   126	        self.tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name)
   127	        self.device = device
   128	        self.attention_matrices = []
   129	        
   130	    def extract_attention(self, layer_id, attention, tokens):
   131	        """Extract attention matrix from a transformer layer."""
   132	        # attention shape: (batch, num_heads, seq_len, seq_len)
   133	        # Average across heads
   134	        attn = attention[0].mean(dim=1)  # (seq_len, seq_len)
   135	        self.attention_matrices.append(attn.detach().cpu().numpy())
   136	    
   137	    def compute_rollout(self, text):
   138	        """Compute attention rollout token importance scores."""
   139	        tokens = self.tokenizer(text, return_tensors="pt", 
   140	                                truncation=True, max_length=512).to(self.device)
   141	        
   142	        self.attention_matrices = []
   143	        
   144	        # Register hook to extract attention from each layer
   145	        hooks = []
   146	        for i, layer in enumerate(self.model.encoder.layer):
   147	            hook = layer.attention.register_forward_hook(
   148	                lambda layer_id=i, attention=None: 
   149	                    self.extract_attention(layer_id, attention, tokens)
   150	            )
   151	            hooks.append(hook)
   152	        
   153	        # Forward pass
   154	        with torch.no_grad():
   155	            output = self.model(**tokens)
   156	        
   157	        # Remove hooks
   158	        for hook in hooks:
   159	            hook.remove()
   160	        
   161	        # Compute rollout product
   162	        A_final = np.eye(len(tokens["input_ids"][0]))
   163	        for A_i in self.attention_matrices:
   164	            A_i = A_i + np.eye(A_i.shape[0])  # Add identity
   165	            A_final = A_final @ A_i
   166	        
   167	        # Normalize and compute importance
   168	        row_sums = A_final.sum(axis=1, keepdims=True)
   169	        S = A_final / row_sums
   170	        importance = S.sum(axis=1)  # Row sums = token importance
   171	        
   172	        return importance, tokens
   173	```
   174	
   175	### 3.3 Expected Output
   176	- Token importance scores for each position in the input
   177	- Higher scores indicate more important tokens
   178	- Can be used to rank and prune tokens
   179	
   180	---
   181	
   182	## Phase 4: Integrated Gradients Implementation (Estimated: 2 hours)
   183	
   184	### 4.1 Method Description
   185	Integrated gradients computes feature importance by integrating gradients along a path from a baseline to the input. For LLMs, this attributes importance to each token based on how much it contributes to the output.
   186	
   187	**Algorithm:**
   188	1. Define baseline (e.g., zero embedding or `<PAD>` token)
   189	2. Create interpolation: `x'(α) = baseline + α × (input - baseline)` for `α ∈ [0,1]`
   190	3. Compute gradients at each interpolation point
   191	4. Integrate: `IG_i = (x_i - x_baseline_i) × ∫₀¹ (∂F/∂x_i)(x'(α)) dα`
   192	5. Sum across layers for final attribution
   193	
   194	### 4.2 Implementation Code
   195	```python
   196	import torch
   197	from captum.attr import IntegratedGradients
   198	from transformers import AutoModel, AutoTokenizer
   199	
   200	class IntegratedGradientsAttribution:
   201	    def __init__(self, model_name="bert-base-uncased", device="cpu"):
   202	        self.model = AutoModel.from_pretrained(model_name).to(device)
   203	        self.tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name)
   204	        self.device = device
   205	        
   206	    def compute_ig(self, text, baseline_text="[PAD]", target_layer=-1):
   207	        """Compute integrated gradients token attributions."""
   208	        # Tokenize input and baseline
   209	        inputs = self.tokenizer(text, return_tensors="pt", 
   210	                                truncation=True, max_length=512).to(self.device)
   211	        baselines = self.tokenizer(baseline_text, return_tensors="pt", 
   212	                                   max_length=512).to(self.device)
   213	        
   214	        # Pad baseline to same length as input
   215	        b_input_ids = baselines["input_ids"].repeat(1, inputs["input_ids"].shape[1])
   216	        b_attention_mask = baselines["attention_mask"].repeat(1, inputs["attention_mask"].shape[1])
   217	        
   218	        # Initialize IG
   219	        ig = IntegratedGradients(self.model)
   220	        
   221	        # Compute attributions
   222	        attributions = ig.attribute(
   223	            inputs={"input_ids": b_input_ids, "attention_mask": b_attention_mask},
   224	            target=target_layer,
   225	            n_steps=50,  # Number of interpolation steps
   226	            internal_batch_size=8
   227	        )
   228	        
   229	        # Extract toke<response clipped><NOTE>Due to the max output limit, only part of this file has been shown to you.    278	```python
   279	def evaluate_on_longbench(method, dataset, model, tokenizer):
   280	    """Evaluate a method on LongBench benchmark."""
   281	    results = {}
   282	    
   283	    for task_type in ["niah", "multidoc_qa", "single_qa", "summary", "code", "knowledge"]:
   284	        task_data = dataset[task_type]
   285	        task_results = []
   286	        
   287	        for example in task_data:
   288	            context = example["context"]
   289	            question = example["question"]
   290	            expected_answer = example["answer"]
   291	            
   292	            # Compress context using the method
   293	            compressed_context = method.compress(context)
   294	            
   295	            # Run model with compressed input
   296	            full_input = f"{compressed_context}\nQuestion: {question}"
   297	            response = model.generate(full_input)
   298	            
   299	            # Evaluate
   300	            score = compute_score(response, expected_answer, task_type)
   301	            task_results.append(score)
   302	        
   303	        results[task_type] = {
   304	            "mean_score": np.mean(task_results),
   305	            "std_score": np.std(task_results),
   306	            "num_examples": len(task_results)
   307	        }
   308	    
   309	    return results

task_type == 'summarization':\n        return {'rouge_l': rouge_l(pred, gold)}\n\n# Aggregate per category × ratio\nfor cat in categories:\n    for ratio in [2,4,8]:\n        cat_metrics = mean(results[cat][ratio]['metrics'])\n        rank = aggregate_rank(cat_metrics)\n```\n\n## PHASE 5: Pre-registered Selection Rule\n```python\n# Rank methods by mean performance across 3 categories ×
